$comment: Facet screen geometry, devices, size classes and density: the single source for the WASM renderer and the panel firmware (tools/gen_layout.mjs -> layout_gen.h: fw::lay:: screen geometry in device px for this build, fw::lyt:: the device / size class / density / token tables for the Layout page). Values are device px: `v` = the 720 x 720 reference panel (1.5x), `1x` = the 480 x 480 panels. Source = Facet main packages/tokens/src/tokens.json `layout` + `devices` + `sizeClass` + `density` (1x = the docs density.1x table) and site docs concepts/screens.md. Only general screen geometry lives here: a screen's own layout values (Media m-*, mv-*, GitHub pr-*, Clock clock-*) arrive with that screen; component sizes (card, tile, list row, dial) stay in space.json under fw::lay::. Grid rule (Darren 2026-10-21): every value a multiple of 4 px at both densities; the docs' 8 px layout grid at 720 is kept where the docs had it.

screen.about: One inset on every side. The header row sits at y = inset; content starts at top and runs to the bottom inset. More space between groups than inside them; rows are separated by hairlines rather than boxes. One hero per screen.

groups.label: Screen frame
groups.about: The frame every screen shares: the inset, where content starts, and the two spacing rhythms (inside a group, between groups).

groups.label: Header zone
groups.about: One row at y = inset across the content width: back button, the screen's label, optional items, the time at the right edge. Items are a gutter apart.

groups.label: Sections and rows
groups.about: A section label sits section-gap above its rows; a list ends with a more row (hairline, caps label, chevron) when it shows only the top items.

groups.label: Overlays
groups.about: Sheets and toasts sit over the screen. A sheet panel starts at sheet-top with the inset on every side; a toast is the content width, toast-h tall, first at toast-top.

inset.use: every side of every screen; the header row starts at y = inset

gutter.use: between items inside a group (cards, tiles, controls, header items)

top.use: where content starts: inset + header row + the header gap

row.use: the header row height (= the back button)

back-gap.use: back button icon to its label (docs size back-gap)

header-time-w.use: the time slot at the header's right edge (docs layout clock-w)

section-gap.use: a section label to its rows

more-row-h.use: the more row at the end of a list (hairline, caps label, chevron)

sheet-top.use: where a sheet panel starts (inset on the other sides)

toast-top.use: the first toast's top (bottom position: ends at the bottom inset)

density.$comment: Density = px per dp (dp ~ CSS px): about 250 ppi is 1.5x, about 170 ppi is 1x. The logical size (px / density) picks the size class; the same logical size gets the same layout whatever the pixel count. One WASM / firmware build per density.

1x.role: own snapped table (`1x`), not a scaled copy
1x.optical: thin weights one step heavier, small text one step up (Darren's V2), so it stays crisp at fewer pixels

sizeClass.$comment: Layout per logical size (dp). A device gets the largest class whose min fits its dp size. Screens choose what they show per class; one hero per screen everywhere.

tall.use: portrait: Home shows more rows; screens stack (hero on top, controls at the bottom)

wide.use: 7 inch landscape: Home 4 x 2; screens get a side column

large.use: 10 inch: wide plus a second pane (a screen beside its list)

devices.$comment: Screens Facet targets. status: target = built for today (workbench device switch), planned = layout class defined, no build yet. mount = how the panel is mounted (the firmware rotates in software; a square layout does not change).

shelly-x1i.name: Shelly Wall Display X1i
shelly-x1i.runs: the 1.5x WASM build in an Android WebView
